Case A

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. The code for that behavior is in place, and the linked ticket APP-91 and the README agree with it.

Merging waits on one thing: a required check, the unit tests, is still running. The watch window ended before it finished, but nothing has failed and no approval or other outside step is missing.

I recommend deliver because one more watch window can see the unit tests finish.

Pick one:
1. deliver - watch the still-running unit tests for one more window, without adding repair attempts, and continue until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - stop the delivery course and post open problems as a review; with none open, nothing is posted.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case B

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. That behavior is covered, and the linked ticket APP-91 and the README agree with it.

Merging waits on one thing: GitHub requires an approving review from someone other than you, and no other reviewer has approved yet. Both required checks passed, but GitHub blocks you from merging, you cannot use an admin override, and no repair, branch update, watch or workflow approval can supply that review.

I recommend stop because only an independent reviewer's approval can unblock this merge, and none of the other choices can provide it.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - only after another reviewer approves: try again, with 10 more repair attempts and 10 more branch updates allowed. Picking it before then changes nothing.
3. assess - stop the delivery course and post open problems as a review; with none open, nothing is posted.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case C

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. The code for that behavior is in place, and the linked ticket APP-91 and the README agree with it.

Merging waits on one thing: a repository maintainer must approve the waiting workflow run before the required unit tests can start. This is the same missing approval that stopped the last attempt, and it has not changed. The repair attempts allowed for this run are also used up. You cannot approve the workflow run yourself, because that needs a maintainer.

I recommend stop because more attempts cannot supply the maintainer approval the unit tests are waiting for.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - allow 10 more repair attempts and 10 more branch updates and try again. Unless a maintainer has approved the workflow run first, it stops again at once.
3. assess - stop the delivery course and post open problems as a review; with none open, nothing is posted.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case D

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR is meant to make the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. Nothing is covered yet, because the endpoint still returns a fixed value; the linked ticket APP-91 and the README describe the intended behavior.

One problem blocks merging: the health endpoint returns a hardcoded version instead of the build version (src/health.ts:8), so callers see a wrong version after every release. Both CI checks passed, but the health_version test in tests/health.test.mjs failed when it ran on this machine. A repair is drafted that reads the existing build-version value instead.

I recommend deliver because the repair is drafted and this is your PR to push.

Pick one:
1. deliver - apply the drafted repair, rebase on main if needed, watch the checks, and repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review comment and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case E

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR by robin makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are a requested reviewer. That behavior is covered, and the linked ticket APP-91 and the README agree with it.

One problem blocks merging: the description says "Reports uptime", but the endpoint returns only the build version (src/health.ts:8). Anyone reading the PR would expect an uptime figure that is not there.
Proposed description change: "Reports uptime" becomes "Reports the build version".

I recommend deliver because the description fix is drafted and needs no decision from robin.

Pick one:
1. deliver - apply the drafted description fix, merge main into the branch if it falls behind, watch the checks, and continue until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review requesting changes and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case F

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR by robin is meant to make the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are a requested reviewer. Nothing is covered yet, because the endpoint's response has no version field; the linked ticket APP-91 and the README describe the intended behavior.

One problem blocks merging: the health endpoint's response is missing the version field (src/health.ts:8), so callers cannot tell which build is running. Both CI checks passed, but the health_version test in tests/health.test.mjs failed when it ran on this machine. Delivery is unavailable because you have read-only access and cannot push to this branch.

I recommend assess because you cannot push a repair yourself, and posting the finding gives robin the concrete fix.

Pick one:
1. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review requesting changes and make no repairs. [recommended]
2. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case G

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/contract-exception recommended=1

Current wording: the service returns the build version at /health.
Proposed wording: the service returns the build version at /status.

Today the spec requires the build version to be served at the existing health address. Moving it to a new address gains nothing for the goal of serving the build version, because the existing health address can already return the same value. I recommend preserve contract because a repair at the existing health address delivers the goal without changing the spec.

Pick one:
1. preserve contract - keep the spec's address requirement and continue repairs that serve the build version there. [recommended]
2. accept contract change - amend the spec to move the build version to the new address, then continue.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: The After wording moved `contract` and `authority` through Case G alone. Before gave a two-sentence explanation with /health inside the recommendation reason and no wording pair. After shows the Current/Proposed wording pair with /health and /status, then exactly three path-free sentences directly above Pick one covering the current requirement, what moving the address gains, and that the existing address can already return the build version; its rows state consequences without arguing. Keep that shape. No fact Before held was lost, but three After drifts in A-F are worth tightening. In Case A the deliver row now says "without adding repair attempts, and continue until merge is offered": it drops the base-branch-update cap and adds an open-ended tail that sits awkwardly beside "exactly one additional watch window", so restore "without adding repair or branch-update attempts" and end the row at the single window. The A-F reports now name the ticket ID (APP-91), and the assess rows say "delivery course"; neither is forbidden by `authority` as written, but both edge toward the IDs and internal terms it guards against, so say "the linked ticket" and "stop delivery". In Case E, keep the description preview as an exact quoted old-to-new pair; "becomes" still preserves it, but do not paraphrase further.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Only the contract fact moved, and it moved as intended. Before's Case G put /health and /status inside the explanatory sentences and showed no wording pair. After shows the current and proposed wordings with their exact paths, then gives three path-free sentences covering the current requirement, the lack of gain from changing the address, and that the existing handler can already return the build version, with preserve contract first, then accept contract change and stop, and neutral row consequences. The other seven facts hold in both outputs, so nothing regressed. Two things in After are worth tightening. First, the Case G explanation of why the existing address already works is folded into the second sentence's 'because' clause, and the third sentence only restates the recommendation; giving that point its own sentence would make the fact more robust. Second, After adds 'You cannot approve your own PR' to Cases A-D and extra standing paragraphs in D and E. These break no fact, since the reason still sits directly above Pick one, but they add prose the Change did not ask for, and if they grow they risk pushing the reason away from Pick one. Keep the Case A deliver row's 'exactly one additional window without extending the repair or sync allowances' and the Case B deliver row's leading 'only after another reviewer approves' condition as they are.
